name: Evidence for a 2014–2015 neutrino flare from TXS 0506+056

significance.quote: Allowing for time-variable flux, this constitutes 3.5{\sigma} evidence for neutrino emission from the direction of TXS 0506+056, independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode.
significance.value: 3.5σ (time-variable flux, excess from the direction of TXS 0506+056)

summary.plain: Searching 9.5 years of IceCube data after the 2017 alert, the collaboration found an excess of high-energy neutrino events at the position of the same blazar between September 2014 and March 2015, which it describes as 3.5σ evidence for neutrino emission from that direction, independent of and prior to the 2017 flare.
summary.technical: Archival time-dependent point-source search of 9.5 years of IceCube data at the position of TXS 0506+056 finds an excess between September 2014 and March 2015 at 3.5σ for a time-variable flux hypothesis.

title: Neutrino emission from the direction of the blazar TXS 0506+056 prior to the IceCube-170922A alert
why_it_matters: The abstract says the 2014–2015 excess is independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode and that this suggests blazars are the first identifiable sources of the high-energy astrophysical neutrino flux.
